chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Dawud ibn Farqad said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Takbir is in every obligatory prayer, and there is no Takbir in the voluntary prayers during the days of Tashriq.'

And the rationale in the first narration is to remove the prohibition for whoever said Takbir after the voluntary prayers, because a person is not prohibited from saying Takbir in all circumstances, so how much more so after the voluntary prayers.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Tashriq, specifically the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah following Eid al-Adha.
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greater), often recited aloud in congregation after prayers.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on saying Takbir in voluntary prayers during the Days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the obligatory and voluntary prayers during the Days of Tashriq, specifying that the distinct communal Takbir applies to the five daily Fard prayers but not to Nafl prayers. This ruling highlights the specific liturgical character of the Tashriq days, where the obligatory prayers serve as the primary vehicle for the public declaration of God's greatness, while voluntary prayers remain unaffected by this specific restriction. The commentary clarifies that this is a specific legal delineation rather than a general prohibition, as Takbir is inherently permissible in all states.
